newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude trade shows differentials holding.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude trade shows differentials holding.

text.p: As action picked up on the wet North Sea market fundamental demand was seen maintaining current strong differentials and some traders felt the current cold snap in Europe would lead to even stronger differentials.
As expected, Tuesday's one Brent cargo was taken from the chains before the five o'clock deadline and was heard offered by the trader at Feb +25 cents against a bid five cents lower.
February Brent on the IPE had gained some 10 cents by 1843 GMT to $24.66 a barrel.
Two Brents traded -- a Jan 19-21 at Feb +20 cents with a refiner picking up a Jan 21-23 later in the day one cent lower.

Other wet activity included an Ekofisk on Jan 28 at dated Brent +25 cents, a Gullfaks (Jan 19-21) at dated +25 and a Jan 27-29 Forties at a healthy dated Brent +43. Only four January Forties cargoes now remained unsold and up to six Ekofisks, traders said.
Many North Sea traders expected U.S. demand to emerge in the short term.

"It looks like the weather is going to get colder over there. If their margins improve they will need to come out and buy and we will see differentials go up. I'm surprised they are as low as they are in fact," one refiner said.
The LR2 of Brent which loads on January 10, destined for the U.S. was heard already committed.
Forties was assessed around dated Brent +40/42 cents.
Brent CFD's action was slow. Next week (Jan 13-17) moved early in the day at Feb +8 cents and later at Feb +10 and March +63 cents.
